chapter_guidelines.content:
Assign a code from category I16, Hypertensive crisis, for documented 
hypertensive urgency, hypertensive emergency or unspecified 
hypertensive crisis. Code also any identified hypertensive disease (I10-
I15). The sequencing is based on the reason for the encounter.
chapter_guidelines.title: Hypertensive Crisis

chapter_guidelines.content:
Uncontrolled hypertension may refer to untreated hypertension or 
hypertension not responding to current therapeutic regimen. In either 
case, assign the appropriate code from categories I10-I15, Hypertensive 
diseases.
chapter_guidelines.title: Hypertension, Uncontrolled

chapter_guidelines.content:
This diagnostic statement usually refers to an existing state of 
hypertension under control by therapy. Assign the appropriate code from 
categories I10-I15, Hypertensive diseases.
chapter_guidelines.title: Hypertension, Controlled

chapter_guidelines.content:
Subcategory H35.0, Background retinopathy and retinal vascular 
changes, should be used along with a code from categories I10 – I15, in 
the Hypertensive diseases section, to include the systemic hypertension. 
The sequencing is based on the reason for the encounter.
chapter_guidelines.title: Hypertensive Retinopathy

chapter_guidelines.content:
Hypertension with heart conditions classified to I50.-, Heart failure, 
I51.4, Myocarditis, unspecified, I51.89, Other ill-defined heart 
diseases, and I51.9, Heart disease, unspecified, is assigned to a code 
from category I11, Hypertensive heart disease. Use additional 
code(s) from category I50, Heart failure, or I51, Complications and 
ill-defined descriptions of heart disease, to identify the heart 
condition.  
 
Hypertension with heart conditions classified to I51.5, Myocardial 
degeneration, or I51.7, Cardiomegaly, is assigned to a code from 
category I11, Hypertensive heart disease. No additional code is 
assigned to identify the specific heart condition.  
 
The same heart conditions (I50.-, I51.4-I51.7, I51.89, I51.9) with 
hypertension are coded separately if the provider has documented they 
are unrelated to the hypertension. The applicable hypertension code 
I10, Essential (primary) hypertension, or a code from category I15, 
Secondary hypertension, should be assigned. Sequence according to 
the circumstances of the admission/encounter.
chapter_guidelines.title: Hypertension with Heart Disease

text:
Encounter Summary:
- 65-year-old male with a 10-year history of hypertension treated with valsartan 80 mg daily.
- Current blood pressure is documented as 132/82.
- Cardiac evaluation notes: "Echocardiogram: LVEF 65%, normal wall motion, no LVH. ECG: sinus rhythm."
- Documented diagnosis: "essential hypertension grade 1 (well controlled), no target organ damage."

Documentation Gaps:
- No clear CDI query opportunity identified from the excerpt.
  - Why it matters: The diagnosis is already documented with adequate specificity for ICD-10-CM hypertension coding in this excerpt.
  - Evidence quote: "Diagnosis: essential hypertension grade 1 (well controlled), no target organ damage."
  - Minimal clarification needed: None required for the documented condition based on the available text.

Proposed Provider Queries:
- None recommended.
  - Reason: The excerpt already supports essential (primary) hypertension, and there is no documented heart disease, CKD, hypertensive crisis, or secondary cause requiring clarification.
  - Supporting evidence:
    - "Diagnosis: essential hypertension grade 1 (well controlled), no target organ damage."
    - "Echocardiogram: LVEF 65%, normal wall motion, no LVH. ECG: sinus rhythm."

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Hypertension type documented: essential/primary.
- Control status documented: well controlled.
- No target organ damage documented.
- No evidence in excerpt of hypertensive heart disease, hypertensive CKD, hypertensive heart/CKD combination, secondary hypertension, or hypertensive crisis.
- ICD-10-CM alignment: essential (primary) hypertension maps to I10.
- Note: "grade 1" is clinically descriptive here but does not create a more specific ICD-10-CM hypertension code in the provided coding references.

Risk Flags:
- No direct contradictions identified in the excerpt.
- "Grade 1" may be terminology used in clinical classification, but for ICD-10-CM the available coding references support I10 for essential (primary) hypertension.
- No unsupported additional diagnoses should be added from this excerpt.

Specialist Trace:
- Medical Coding Expert: Consulted.
  - Requested: Review for coding specificity, CDI gaps, and compliant query opportunities.
  - Accepted: Essential (primary) hypertension corresponds to ICD-10-CM I10; chapter guidelines indicate controlled hypertension is still coded from I10-I15, and no evidence supports hypertensive heart disease/CKD/crisis categories here.
  - Rejected/unused: No unsupported expansion to other hypertensive diagnoses because the chart excerpt does not document them.
